_meta.purpose: Indicative premiums and rules of thumb for the protection tools: how much life cover, how much health cover, and whether to keep a traditional policy.
_meta.health_warning: Premiums here are indicative ranges for a healthy non-smoker buying online, not quotes. Your own premium depends on medicals, occupation, smoking, city and insurer, and is fixed for the whole term at the age you buy.

confidence_key.corroborated: Several insurer and aggregator tables agree on the range.
confidence_key.indicative: A representative middle of published ranges; treat as an order of magnitude.

term_life._note: Annual premium per Rs 1 crore of cover, level term to age 60-65, healthy non-smoker buying online. Male rates; women typically pay 10-15% less. Rates rise steeply with age, which is the whole argument for buying early.
rules: Cover should run until the year your dependants stop needing your income: usually your retirement age, not longer.
Buy plain term. Return-of-premium versions cost roughly twice as much for the same cover; the difference invested does better.
Declare every illness, every prescription and every claim honestly. Non-disclosure is the main reason claims are rejected, and section 45 protects the policy only after three years.
One insurer or two, it does not matter; what matters is that the nominee knows the policy exists.

health._note: Family floater premiums, indicative, for a healthy family buying online in a metro. A super top-up sits above a deductible and is far cheaper per rupee of cover than raising the base.
rules: Employer cover ends the day the job does, and it rarely follows you into your fifties when you need it. Hold your own policy alongside it.
A base policy plus a super top-up costs much less than one large policy for the same total cover.
Buy before the first diagnosis: waiting periods for pre-existing conditions run two to four years, and a new condition can make you uninsurable.
Check room-rent limits, co-pay, and the day-care and restoration clauses before the premium.
Parents are cheaper to cover on a separate policy than on your floater, and the 80D limit for senior-citizen parents is separate.

traditional_policy._note: Endowment, money-back and similar participating policies. Bonus rates are the simple reversionary bonus per Rs 1,000 of sum assured a year, as declared by large insurers in recent years; the final additional bonus is paid only at maturity on long policies.
traditional_policy.paid_up_rule: Stop paying and the sum assured falls to sum assured x premiums paid / premiums payable; bonuses already attached stay, no new bonus accrues, and the reduced amount is paid at maturity.
traditional_policy.surrender_rule: Guaranteed surrender value is a percentage of premiums paid that rises with policy year; most insurers pay a higher special surrender value which also includes part of the attached bonuses. IRDAI's 2024 rules raised early-year values.
traditional_policy.maturity_tax: Proceeds are exempt under section 10(10D) only if the annual premium never exceeds 10% of the sum assured (20% for policies issued before 1 April 2012). Since 1 April 2023, proceeds from policies with aggregate annual premium above Rs 5 lakh are taxable as other income.
rules: A traditional policy is a savings product with a small amount of insurance attached. Judge it on its return, and buy the insurance separately.
Money already paid is gone either way; the only question is what the future premiums do next.
Never surrender term cover you may not be able to replace: check you are insurable before you give up a policy.
Surrendering within two years usually returns nothing at all.

sources.what: Section 10(10D) and the Rs 5 lakh premium rule
